scope: Shopify Payments card rates and third-party transaction fees for US stores by plan. Subscriptions are shown as context, not per-sale; POS Pro, Plus custom rates and Shop Pay Installments are out of scope.
structure: Two separate fees. (1) Shopify Payments card processing: fee = rate x amount + fixed cents, charged when you capture payment; the rate depends on plan (Basic / Grow / Advanced / Plus) and channel — online standard cards 2.9% / 2.7% / 2.5% (+ 30¢), online premium cards (commercial/corporate/business cards and all domestic Amex) 3.5% / 3.3% / 3.1% (+ 30¢), in-person cards 2.6% / 2.5% / 2.4% (+ 10¢), in-person manual entry 3.5% + 10¢ on every plan; cards issued outside the US add 1% ('cross-border fee'); paying in a non-payout currency adds a 1.5% currency conversion fee (US). The loaded pages do not itemize the base for card fees beyond 'the payment for an order' (i.e. the captured order amount). (2) Third-party transaction fee, charged by Shopify only when a third-party payment provider processes the payment (or on the store-credit/gift-card portion for stores created on or after May 12, 2025): 2% / 1% / 0.6% / 0.2% of [(cost of products - discounts) + tax + shipping charges]; waived entirely when Shopify Payments is the sole provider; if Shopify Payments runs alongside a third-party provider, Shopify Payments transactions also carry a 1.25% premium. Neither card fees nor third-party fees are returned on refunds. No rounding rule is published.

There are no setup fees on any of our plans.
Third-party transaction fees may apply when you use a third-party payment provider (instead of Shopify Payments). The rate depends on your plan.
Shopify charges a small fee to allow you to accept major credit cards, such as Visa and Mastercard, as payment in your store. These fees vary depending on the plan that you choose.

Aside from the credit card rate and the subscription fees for your store's Shopify subscription plan, there are no monthly fees, no hidden fees, and no setup fees for Shopify Payments. When you use Shopify Payments as your sole payment provider, there are no third-party transaction fees for orders.

Transactions processed by your third-party provider, such as credit and debit card payments, are subject to third-party transaction fees based on your Shopify plan.
Transactions processed by Shopify Payments, such as Shop Pay and local payment methods, are charged at standard Shopify Payments rates plus a 1.25% premium. Shopify Payments rates vary by plan type and market.

Standard: Includes domestic consumer cards issued by Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and Diners Club.
Premium: Includes domestic commercial, corporate, or business-tier cards, such as Visa Business, and all domestic American Express cards.
If you process international cards and payment methods, then an additional charge applies above the base rate.

If your online store is based in the United States and you process payments by using Shopify Payments, then you're charged a 1% cross-border fee on all sales made with a credit card issued in another country.
Manually entered payments are subject to higher fees because card details are often collected over the phone or through other unencrypted methods, increasing the risk of fraud.

Shopify uses this formula to calculate third-party transaction fees for a 30-day period:
[(cost of products - discounts) + tax + shipping charges] x rate
The rate for third-party transaction charges varies depending on your pricing plan.

Transaction fees don't apply for POS orders or for manual payment methods, which include cash on delivery (COD), bank deposits, checks, test orders, and draft orders marked as paid or pending. Third-party transaction fees aren't returned to you when you issue an order refund.
Transaction fees are in addition to processing fees charged by your third-party payment provider.

Stores on the Shopify Plus plan that use Shopify Payments as their sole payment provider have their third-party transaction fees waived, including fees on store credit and gift cards. If you use Shopify Payments alongside a third-party payment provider, then transaction fees apply.
Credit card transaction fees aren't returned to you when you issue a refund.
If you switch to an annual billing cycle, then you can receive a discount on your subscription charge. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate.

When you use Shopify Payments, you pay the credit card rate, but you don't pay a transaction fee. Stores that use a third-party payment provider instead of Shopify Payments pay both a transaction fee from Shopify, and credit card fees charged by their third-party payment provider.

When you capture the payment for an order, you're charged a Shopify Payments fee (in your payout currency) which covers the cost of processing the payment. The fee amount depends on the type of credit card that is used and the location where the credit card is registered.
| Currency conversion fee | 1.5% | 2% | 2% |

Currency conversion fee - The fee that Shopify charges (in your payout currency) to convert currencies when you capture a payment. Currency conversion fees and credit card fees are not returned to you when you issue a refund, but you're not charged additional conversion fees when you issue a refund or when you receive a chargeback.

notes: The pricing page defaults to the 'Pay yearly' toggle, so the headline prices ($29 / $79 / $299) are the annual-billing effective monthly rates; monthly billing is $39 / $105 / $399. Plus is 'Starts at $2,300 USD/mo' with 'Not included' under Pay yearly and a 'Try for $399' offer.
Plus card rate conflict: the plan card says 'Card rates from 2.25% + 30¢ USD' while every Plus row of the comparison table says 'Most competitive rates' (no number).

The base for Shopify Payments card fees is not itemized on the loaded pages (fees are charged 'when you capture the payment for an order'); the third-party transaction fee formula explicitly includes tax and shipping. Calculator author must decide whether to apply card rates to the order total including shipping and tax (consistent with fees on the captured amount).

'Online international rates + 1%' on the pricing page corresponds to the help center's '1% cross-border fee on all sales made with a credit card issued in another country' for US stores; the pricing page lists it only under online rates, so treatment of international cards in person is unspecified.
Online 'premium' card rates apply to domestic commercial/corporate/business cards and all domestic American Express cards — a calculator needs the card type as an input.

Third-party transaction fees also apply to the store-credit/gift-card portion of orders for stores created on or after May 12, 2025, even when Shopify Payments is used (waived on Plus with Shopify Payments as sole provider).
If Shopify Payments is used alongside a third-party provider, Shopify Payments transactions are charged standard rates plus a 1.25% premium.
Currency conversion fee is 1.5% for US stores (2% France/other; 3% for PayPal Wallet) and is charged in the payout currency; it is not refunded on refunds.
No rounding rule is published on the loaded pages.
help.shopify.com returns an empty shell over plain HTTP; the pages were captured with a JavaScript-rendering fetch.
Rates shown are for the USA | English locale; the page says pricing and payment options differ by country.
summary: With Shopify Payments, online card payments cost 2.9% + 30¢ on Basic, 2.7% on Grow and 2.5% on Advanced (premium cards 3.5%/3.3%/3.1%), in person 2.6%/2.5%/2.4% + 10¢, plus 1% for cards issued outside the US. Using another payment provider adds Shopify's 2%/1%/0.6% transaction fee on top of that provider's charges. Plans are $39/$105/$399 a month.
